name: Adirondack Community Foundation Terrestrial Invasive Species Management Grant
summary: Grants of up to $5,000 to nonprofits and municipalities for managing terrestrial invasive species in the Adirondack region, including direct removal and training or support for residents and organisations.

amount.note: Distributed over two years, contingent on a one-year follow-up report

reporting: Recipients submit a follow-up report after one year; the second payment depends on it.

calls.label: Annual round (applications by April 30)
calls.recurring: Applications are due by April 30 each year.

status.quote: Applications must be received by April 30th annually.

recurring.quote: Applications must be received by April 30th annually.

applicant_types.quote: grants are available to nonprofit organizations and municipalities to support projects working to manage terrestrial invasive species

geography.quote: the Adirondack region, defined for this purpose by Adirondack Community Foundation as all of Clinton, Essex, Franklin, and Hamilton counties

window.quote: Applications must be received by April 30th annually.

amount.quote: Grants will be up to $5,000, distributed over two years contingent on a one year follow up report.

reporting.quote: As part of this grant, we ask recipients to submit a follow-up report.
